Subject: Recap + next steps from today's discovery (latency/throughput focus)

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap so we’re aligned and to make it easy to share with your stakeholders: 

- Goal: Replace in-house transformer endpoint for product search ranking with a lower-latency, cost-predictable inference layer. 
- Primary constraints you flagged: P99 latency under 250ms for 512-token sequences, peak concurrent requests ~120 RPS, and strict data isolation for PII.
- Action items I captured:
  1) Redwood to run a short bench with your sample workload (we requested rn-workload-sample.csv).
  2) Marcus will answer the two kernel/precision questions you raised about quantized FP16 behavior and KV cache warmup.
  3) RetailNova to confirm target SLA/commit window and whether you'd like a Dedicated pilot or hosted evaluation.

Attachments: rn-workload-sample.csv (CSV, 45KB) — thanks for sending this in the call.

Next steps: Marcus plans to send the bench readout and short writeup by tomorrow EOD PST. After you review the numbers we can schedule a 30-min follow-up to decide pilot scope.

If priority shifted or timing changed, just say the word — happy to adjust cadence.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@retailnova.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 11:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from today's discovery (latency/throughput focus)

Hi Sam / Neha —

Per our call, I ran the workload from rn-workload-sample.csv against the LlamaX-13B quantized profile we discussed. Summary below; full PDF attached.

Summary (key numbers):
- Median token latency (1-token inc): 48ms
- P95 token latency: 110ms
- P99 end-to-end (512 tokens): 190ms (single-request, non-batched)
- Throughput: sustained 110 RPS with batching window tuned to 6ms; burst tested to 160 RPS with moderate latency uplift (~+30ms P99)
- Observations: KV cache warmup added ~18ms on first few requests for cold sessions; amortizes quickly with session stickiness. Quantized FP16 showed negligible quality delta on our eval set; we used per-channel quantization and mixed-kernel FP16 for matmul.

Attachments: redwood-latency-readout-20260910.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB) — includes CSV export of the run and config snippet.

Notes on isolation: We can run the pilot in a dedicated VPC with customer-managed keys; that path introduces a small cold-start penalty for the first pod spin but preserves full isolation.

Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the PDF — otherwise tell me what pieces you want us to expand.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
